$comment: Which client model implements which OpenAPI schema. Read by scripts/contract-check.mjs.
Explicit rather than inferred: nothing links `meSchema` to `MeResponse` by name, and guessing the
pairing would produce confident nonsense. A model absent from this file is NOT validated, and the
checker reports coverage so that absence stays visible instead of reading as a pass.
COVERAGE GAP — CLOSED. This file previously recorded that PublicProfileView and IdentityStatusView
returned anonymous objects, had no schema, and so could not be listed. Both are now typed, as are
the twelve profile sub-resources that were still projecting through hand-written mappers, and all
of them appear below. The wire did not move: PublicCertificateCard keeps `issued_at` via
[JsonPropertyName] because the mapper renamed it from CreatedAt, and the Journey keeps its nested
`evidence` object and constant `source` as JourneyNodeView. Those two are the reason this expansion
is worth more than it looks — both are shapes a naive 'just return the record' would have broken
silently, and both are now pinned by a mapping below rather than by a comment.
GATE STRENGTH, measured rather than assumed — and now fixed. Swashbuckle used to emit `required` on
36 of 266 schemas (53 entries in total), so two of contract-check's checks — missing_required and
optionality — were inert and only unknown_field was live. The cause was that the intended switch,
SchemaGeneratorOptions.NonNullableReferenceTypesAsRequired, does not exist in the pinned Swashbuckle
6.6.2; it arrived in 6.7.0, and setting it was a compile error. RequiredFromNonNullableSchemaFilter
re-implements it against the nullability Swashbuckle already computes. The spec now carries required
on 245 of 290 schemas (808 entries), and the two dormant checks report 31 real findings where they
previously reported none. scripts/contract-check.test.mjs asserts each category still fires, so a
future regression to the inert state fails a test instead of reading as a clean pass.

models.$why: Bug #3 lived here: the wire nests these under `trust`, web declared can_organize_paid flat with .default(false), so paid hosting read as unavailable to every user on every request.
The nested half of the same bug. Reused by the endpoint rather than re-projected, so one definition serves both.

D-292: web declared camelCase against a snake_case API, every parse threw, and /chats caught it and rendered 'No event chats' for everyone. The fix kept camelCase models behind a camelizeKeys() adapter, so this pair is validated through that transform — the field names here are post-normalisation, not wire keys.

The profile root. Typed in this pass; previously an anonymous object, so the platform's most-read public page had no contract at all. Its nested members are mapped separately below — that is what makes a nested mismatch visible rather than hidden inside the parent.

The renamed key. The mapper emitted CreatedAt as `issued_at`; both clients bind `issued_at`, so returning the record raw would have silently become `created_at`. Mapped so the attribute that preserves it can never be dropped unnoticed.
The re-nested shape. The wire carries `source` plus an `evidence` object that the flat JourneyNode does not have; JourneyNodeView is that shape given a name.

Nested members of PublicProfileView. Mapped individually because contract-check compares one schema to one client model — a mismatch inside `stats` or `verification` is invisible from the parent, which only sees that the key exists.
